st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden, then stir in the turmeric.
Add the lamb, salt and pepper and brown for 6 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide pan. Fry the parsley, cilantro and scallions for 15 minutes, stirring often, until very dark green and fragrant.
Add the fenugreek leaves for the last 2 minutes of frying. Do not let them burn.
Stir the fried herbs, kidney beans and dried limes into the lamb.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour more until the lamb is very tender and the oil rises to the top.
Taste. Press a lime against the pot for more sourness, and discard the limes if the stew turns bitter. Serve over rice.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until fragrant. Let them cool.
Grind the walnuts in a food processor into a fine, damp crumb, but stop before they turn to paste.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 8 minutes with the turmeric until golden.
Add the chicken, salt and pepper and brown lightly for 5 minutes per side. Remove the chicken.
Add the walnuts and [[2 cup]] water to the pot. Simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring often, until the oils darken the sauce.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses, sugar and cinnamon.
Return the chicken and add the remaining [[0.5 cup]] water. Cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes until the chicken reaches 175°F (80°C) and is tender.
Taste and balance with a little more sugar or molasses. Serve over steamed rice.

ing: 80 percent lean, or beef and lamb mix
st: Mix the beef, onion, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, pepper and baking soda. Knead by hand for 5 minutes until sticky. Chill for 30 minutes.
Dissolve the saffron in the hot water and set aside.
Boil a large pot of water with [[2 tbsp]] salt. Add the soaked, drained rice and boil for 6 minutes until the grains are soft outside and firm inside. Drain.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in the pot, spoon in the rice, and poke a few holes in it. Cover the lid with a towel and steam on low for 25 minutes.
Mix a spoonful of the rice with the saffron water. Spoon it over the top of the rice.
Wet your hands and press the meat onto flat skewers into long, thin strips with fingerprint ridges. Heat the grill or broiler to high.
Cook the kebabs for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and 160°F (71°C) inside. Grill the tomatoes at the same time until charred.
Melt the remaining [[4 tbsp]] butter and drizzle over the rice. Serve with the kebabs, tomatoes and a dusting of sumac.
Dissolve the saffron in the hot water and let it steep for 10 minutes.
Mix the onion, yogurt, lemon juice, oil, salt, pepper and half of the saffron water.
Add the chicken and coat well. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Thread the chicken onto metal or soaked wooden skewers, leaving a little space between the pieces.
Heat a grill to medium-high, or the oven broiler on high.
Cook the skewers for 12 to 15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until browned and 165°F (74°C) inside.
Mix the remaining saffron water with the melted butter and brush over the hot skewers.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with rice and grilled tomatoes.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with [[2 tbsp]] salt. Add the drained rice and boil for 6 minutes until soft outside and still firm in the center. Drain.
Dissolve the saffron in the hot water and let it steep for 5 minutes.
Mix [[1 cup]] of the cooked rice with the yogurt and [[2 tbsp]] of the saffron water.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a nonstick pot over medium heat.
Spread the yogurt rice evenly over the bottom of the pot, pressing flat.
Mound the remaining rice on top in a pyramid and poke 5 holes down to the bottom with a spoon handle.
Drizzle with the rest of the butter. Wrap the lid in a towel and cover. Cook on medium for 5 minutes, then low for 45 minutes.
Set the pot in a sink with a little cold water for 1 minute to loosen the crust. Flip onto a plate to see the golden crust.

ing: or sour cream mixed with a little salt
st: Drain the soaked chickpeas and kidney beans. Put them in a large pot with the water, one sliced onion and the turmeric.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 1 hour, until the beans start to soften. Add the lentils for the last 20 minutes.
Add the spinach, parsley, cilantro and scallions, with the salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the noodles and cook for 10 minutes until tender, stirring so they do not clump.
For the toppings, fry the remaining onion in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 12 minutes until deep brown. Set half aside.
Fry the garlic in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 1 minute until golden, then off the heat stir in the mint.
Stir the onion half into the soup and taste for salt. Thin with hot water if too thick.
Ladle into bowls. Top with the swirl of kashk, fried onion, garlic and mint.

ing: or thick plain yogurt thinned with a squeeze of lemon
st: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Prick the eggplants with a fork and roast on a tray for 40 minutes, turning once, until collapsed and charred.
Cool slightly, peel off the skins, and drain the pulp in a colander for 5 minutes.
Fry the onion in [[2 tbsp]] oil with the turmeric for 12 minutes until deep golden. Set half aside for topping.
Add the garlic to the pan with the remaining onion and cook for 1 minute.
Chop the eggplant pulp and add to the pan with the salt and pepper. Mash and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in half the kashk and [[1 tsp]] of the mint. Remove from heat.
Fry the remaining mint in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 30 seconds, then take it off the heat.
Spread the dip on a plate. Top with kashk, fried onion, mint oil and walnuts. Serve with bread.
Dissolve the saffron in the hot water and steep for 10 minutes.
Cook the onion in [[1 tbsp]] butter for 6 minutes. Add the chicken, [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper and turmeric and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the broth and half of the saffron water. Cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Boil the rice in a large pot of water with [[2 tbsp]] salt for 6 minutes. Drain.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pot, then layer in the rice, poke steam holes, wrap the lid in a towel, and steam on low for 30 minutes.
Sizzle the barberries in [[2 tbsp]] butter for 1 minute, stir in [[1 tbsp]] sugar, and cook 30 seconds more. Do not burn.
Stir a spoon of rice with the remaining saffron water to make a golden rice.
Heap the rice on a platter, top with the saffron rice and barberries, and serve with the chicken.
Char the whole eggplants directly over a gas flame or under a hot broiler for 20 minutes, turning, until the skin is blackened and the inside is soft.
Cool, peel off the skin, and mash the flesh with a fork. Drain any bitter liquid.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Fry the garlic for 1 minute until just golden.
Add the turmeric, tomato paste and tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the eggplant, salt and pepper and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and the oil separates.
Make a well and pour in the eggs. Stir gently for 3 minutes until the eggs are fully cooked.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve warm with flatbread.

ing: ground, steeped in 3 tbsp hot water
st: Put the rice and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Simmer partly covered for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is very soft and broken down.
Stir in the sugar and cook for 10 minutes more. The pudding should be thick.
Add the saffron with its water and the butter. Stir for 10 minutes on low heat.
Stir in the rose water and cardamom, then cook for 5 minutes until it is thick enough to hold a spoon.
Spoon into small bowls or one shallow dish and smooth the top.
Cool for 30 minutes. Decorate with lines of cinnamon and the almonds.
Chill if you like, and serve at room temperature or cold.
Boil the sugar and water for 5 minutes until syrupy. Remove from heat and cool completely.
Stir the rose water into the syrup.
Cook the vermicelli in boiling water for 3 minutes until soft. Drain, rinse in cold water, and cut into short 2 inch lengths.
Mix the noodles with the cold syrup in a shallow freezer-safe dish.
Freeze for 2 hours, then scrape with a fork to break up the ice crystals.
Freeze again for another 2 hours, scraping every hour, until it forms a slushy, icy sorbet.
Let it sit at room temperature for 10 minutes before serving so it softens a bit.
Scoop into bowls and serve with the lime juice, extra rose water if you like, and pistachios.
Mix the flour, yeast and salt in a bowl, add the warm water and stir to a sticky dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes until doubled.
Make the glaze: whisk [[1 tbsp]] flour into [[0.5 cup]] water in a small pot and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thick. Cool.
Preheat the oven to 450°F with a baking sheet inside. Divide the dough into 2 pieces and rest 10 minutes.
Stretch each piece into a long oval about 12 by 5 inches, then press 3 or 4 deep lines lengthwise with oiled fingertips. Brush all over with glaze and sprinkle with the seeds.
Bake on the hot sheet for 12 minutes until deep golden. Serve warm, torn into strips.
nt: Baked at 450°F on a hot tray
Best swap: use more sesame seeds, same amount, in place of the nigella seeds if you cannot find them.

st: If your chickpea flour is raw, toast [[1.5 cups]] in a dry pan over low heat for 6 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty. Cool.
Heat the oven to 325°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Sift the flour, [[0.75 cup]] powdered sugar, [[1 tsp]] cardamom and a pinch of salt together into a bowl.
Add [[0.5 cup]] melted butter and [[1 tbsp]] rosewater and mix until the dough holds when pressed in your hand.
Roll walnut sized balls and flatten slightly into rounds 0.5 inch thick on the sheet.
Press a few slivers of pistachio onto each cookie. Chill the tray 15 minutes so they do not spread.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes; they should stay pale. Cool completely on the sheet before moving, as they are very fragile.
nt: Baked at 325°F, kept pale
Best swap: use coconut oil 1:1 for the butter for a dairy-free version, or orange blossom water for rosewater.

st: Combine [[2 cup]] sugar and [[1 cup]] water in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves completely.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes without stirring until the syrup is lightly thickened.
Add [[0.5 cup]] white wine vinegar and half the mint sprigs. Simmer 5 more minutes; the syrup should coat a spoon thinly.
Remove from heat, discard the mint and let the syrup cool fully, about 30 minutes. It keeps in the fridge for weeks.
Fill glasses with ice. Add about [[3 tbsp]] syrup per glass, top with cold water and stir well.
Garnish with fresh mint and grated cucumber, or serve with romaine lettuce wedges for dipping in the syrup as is traditional.
nt: Simmered into a syrup, served cold with water and ice
Best swap: if you have no white wine vinegar, use rice vinegar at the same amount; sweeten less for a sharper drink.

st: Wash the grapes, plums, figs and cucumbers in a large bowl of cool water. Drain and dry them on a clean towel to get rid of any surface dirt.
Soak the almonds in cold water for 1 hour, then slip off the skins. This is the traditional way to serve almonds on a guest platter.
Cut the pomegranate in quarters and, over a bowl of water, pry out the arils with your thumbs. The white pith floats and the arils sink, so skim and drain.
Peel the cucumbers if the skin is bitter and cut them lengthwise into quarters, serving them with a pinch of salt on the side.
Halve the figs through the stem, and arrange the green plums in a small bowl with [[1 tsp]] salt for dipping, as is common in Iran.
Mound the nuts in separate piles on a large round tray. Place the grapes, figs and pomegranate arils around the edge.
Tuck the mint among the fruit and serve right away with tea. Guests help themselves.
nt: Don't cook: wash, cut and arrange
Best swap: dried apricots or fresh grapes for fresh figs, and sour green plums can be replaced by green grapes with salt.

st: Rinse the herbs and scallions in cold water. Spin or pat completely dry, so that they stay crisp.
Pick the herb leaves from the thick stems, keeping them in whole sprigs. Pile into a bowl or on a plate with the radishes and scallions.
Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4 minutes, shaking often, until they smell nutty and darken a shade. Cool.
Stir the yogurt with the cucumber, dried mint and a pinch of salt. This is mast-o-khiar. Chill until serving.
Put the feta slabs on a plate and add the toasted walnuts to a small bowl.
Bring the herbs, feta, walnuts, mast-o-khiar and warm bread to the table. To eat, wrap a slab of cheese with a handful of herbs and walnuts in bread.
nt: Mostly raw; walnuts toasted in a dry pan; bread warmed
Best swap: any soft brined white cheese for feta; use thick coconut yogurt for dairy-free mast-o-khiar.

st: Heat the oven to 450°F. Pierce the eggplants and roast on a tray, turning once, until blackened and collapsed, about 40 minutes. A grill or gas flame also works.
Cool slightly, peel off the skin and chop the flesh coarsely, draining any bitter liquid.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the garlic with the turmeric for 1 minute until golden at the edges but not brown.
Add the grated tomato and cook 5 minutes until the juices reduce.
Stir in the eggplant, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Cook, mashing, for 8 minutes until it forms a thick paste.
Make a space and add the eggs. Stir them in and cook until they set to 160°F, about 2 minutes. Serve hot with bread or rice.
nt: Roasted, then pan-cooked
Best swap: leave out the eggs for a vegan version, or use 1 tbsp tomato paste if tomatoes are out of season.

st: Wash the cucumbers and tomatoes. Cut the cucumbers into small cubes about 1/4 inch wide and put them in a large bowl.
Cut the tomatoes in half, scoop out most of the seeds with a spoon, then dice the flesh to the same small size and add to the bowl.
Finely dice the red onion. Rinse it in cold water for 1 minute and drain well to soften the bite, then add to the bowl.
Add the parsley and rub the dried mint between your palms over the bowl to release its aroma.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] lime juice with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper, and pour over the vegetables.
Toss gently and rest for 10 minutes so the juices mingle. Taste, adjust the salt and serve cold alongside kebab or rice.
nt: Don't cook: just chop and toss
Best swap: lemon juice in equal amount for lime, or use 1 tbsp fresh mint for each 1 tbsp dried mint.

ing: finely minced, soaked in cold water
st: Mince the shallots very finely and soak in cold water for 10 minutes to soften the sharpness, then drain well.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and whisk until smooth.
Stir in the drained shallots, the grated garlic and salt.
Crush the dried mint between your palms and stir in half of it.
Taste and add salt or garlic if needed. Chill for 30 minutes.
Drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil, sprinkle with the rest of the mint and the walnuts, and serve with flatbread or kebab.
nt: Don't cook: mix and chill
Best swap: 1 small sweet onion plus extra garlic if you cannot find shallots, or thick coconut yogurt for dairy-free.

ing: ground, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
st: Soak the rinsed rice in warm water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 30 minutes, then drain.
Boil a big pot of water with [[1 tsp]] salt and add the rice. Cook 6 to 7 minutes until a grain bends but is still firm in the center. Drain and rinse with warm water.
Toss the cooked rice gently with all the chopped herbs. Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in the pot, then spoon in the rice in a mound. Poke 5 holes with a spoon handle to the bottom.
Wrap the pot lid in a clean towel and set it on tight. Cook over low heat for 40 minutes until fluffy and steaming. Drizzle the saffron water over a corner of the rice at the end.
Meanwhile, rub the fish with the turmeric, lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Rest for 15 minutes, then pat dry and dredge in the flour.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the fish 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and 145°F inside.
Heap the herb rice on a platter, tuck the fish alongside, and serve with lemon wedges.
nt: Parboiled rice steamed on low, fish pan-fried
Best swap: use 1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves in place of 1 bunch of the herbs if fresh is scarce.

st: Prick the eggplants with a fork and steam or boil them for 10 minutes until completely soft. Drain well and let cool.
Chop the cooled eggplant into small pieces and squeeze out as much liquid as you can with a clean towel.
Bring [[2 cups]] vinegar, [[1 cup]] water, [[1 tbsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] turmeric to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes. Cool fully.
In a big bowl, combine the eggplant, grated carrot, celery, parsley, cilantro, garlic and [[2 tbsp]] dried mint.
Pack the mixture tightly into clean jars, pressing out air pockets. Pour in the cooled vinegar mixture to cover by half an inch.
Close the jars and keep them in a cool dark spot for at least 2 weeks (up to 3) before opening, shaking gently every few days.
nt: Steamed eggplant then vinegar pickled; needs at least 2 weeks to mature
Best swap: any long eggplant works; use 1 tbsp dried mint if fresh herbs are scarce, or skip the celery.

st: Brown the onions in [[2 tbsp]] oil over medium heat for 20 minutes until deep golden. Set half aside for topping.
Add the meat, [[1 tsp]] turmeric and salt to the remaining onions. Cook 10 minutes, add water to cover, and simmer 45 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile boil the lentils in water for 15 minutes until just tender but whole. Drain.
Boil the soaked rice in salted water for 6 to 8 minutes until it bends but is firm in the center. Drain.
Coat a pot with [[2 tbsp]] oil. Layer half the rice, the lentils and meat, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, then the remaining rice in a mound.
Poke steam holes, drizzle the saffron water, wrap the lid in a towel and steam on low for 40 minutes.
Warm the raisins and dates with a splash of oil in a pan for 2 minutes. Serve the rice topped with fruit and reserved onions.
nt: Parboiled then steamed in a covered pot
Best swap: use green lentils or drained canned lentils, and skip the meat with extra onions for vegetarian.
